features.name: Leaf veins
features.blurb: Veins carry water in and sugar out of the leaf. Fine veins branch until no cell is far from one.

features.name: Leaf cells
features.blurb: Each green box is a living cell packed with chloroplasts. Cell walls give the leaf its tiled look.

features.name: Grain facets
features.blurb: Each grain is a tiny rock with its own shape. Clear grains are mostly quartz, the stuff of good glass.

features.name: Pond alga
features.blurb: Spirogyra grows as long green threads, one cell after another. Its spiral chloroplast is a ribbon wound around each cell.

features.name: Bacteria
features.blurb: These rod-shaped cells are about a thousandth of a millimetre long. Your good glass and oil finally let you resolve them.

features.name: Virus particles
features.blurb: Viruses are a hundred times smaller than a pond alga cell. Visible light is too coarse to resolve them, so you need electrons.

features.name: Petal hairs
features.blurb: Tiny hairs cover petals and stems. They slow the wind at the surface and keep small pests off.

features.name: Pollen grains
features.blurb: Each pollen grain carries half of a plant's genes inside a tough shell. The spikes and ridges on that shell are different for every species.

features.name: Wing veins
features.blurb: Veins stiffen the thin wing like the spokes of an umbrella. They also carry fluid and air tubes to keep the wing alive.

features.name: Wing scales
features.blurb: A butterfly's colors come from thousands of overlapping scales, like roof tiles. Each scale is only about twenty micrometres wide.

features.name: Quartz facets
features.blurb: Quartz grains are clear and have sharp, glassy faces. That purity makes quartz sand the best raw material for lenses.

features.name: Surface pits
features.blurb: Wind and water slowly pit the surface of sand grains as they tumble. Pits this small only show up under an oil-immersion lens.
